name: Pokhara Paragliding

difficulty.notes: Tandem flight with a licensed pilot; no experience needed. Take-off is a few running steps down a slope.

duration_days.basis: half-day activity in Pokhara (hotel pick-up to drop-off, ~3 h; ~20-30 min airborne)
duration_days.notes: Longer 45-60 min 'cross-country' tandem flights are offered by some operators. Solo flying has been suspended since 2022.

max_altitude_point: Sarangkot launch ridge (historic main take-off; see notes on current sites)
end_point: Khapaudi landing, north shore of Phewa Lake

itinerary.route: Hotel pick-up - jeep to launch ridge (Toripani / Sarangkot) - briefing and harness - tandem flight over Pokhara valley and Phewa Lake - land at Khapaudi - transfer to hotel
itinerary.notes: Commercial flight window set by CAAN: 11:00-16:30 (extended from 11:00-15:00 in May 2025).

best_seasons.notes: NTB: flights operate almost year-round except the monsoon (June-August). Winter is flyable with cooler mornings.

guide_requirements: Fly only with a CAAN-authorised commercial paragliding company. CAAN regulates paragliding through the Nepal Air Sports Association (NAA), which licenses pilots and companies (pilot licences issued since 2018). CAAN directives require rescue boats (incl. a motorboat) on Phewa Lake during flight hours, drug/alcohol testing of pilots and public display of passenger fees. Operators must hold at least five gliders.

drives: Lakeside - launch ridge by jeep (~20-30 min)
logistics.notes: Site history: after Pokhara International Airport opened (2023) take-off moved from Sarangkot to Mandredhunga with landing at Pame; take-off later moved to Toripani; from 22 May 2025 landings returned to Khapaudi on Phewa's shore. Confirm the exact launch site at booking.

highlights: Views of Annapurna range, Machhapuchhre, Dhaulagiri and Manaslu from the air
Glide over Pokhara valley and land beside Phewa Lake
Pokhara described by NAA as South Asia's paragliding capital; paragliding began here in 2000
risks: Inherent air-sport risk; flights cancelled in rain, high wind or poor visibility
Airspace restrictions from Pokhara International Airport can change launch/landing sites
unverified: Current take-off sites conflict: Republica (May 2025) says take-off remains Toripani; HimalPress and an operator say Sarangkot and Toripani (operator adds Bahakot); the NAA website lists Sarangkot as 'temporary suspense'. Treat Sarangkot as the historic site and confirm at booking.
Sarangkot launch altitude 1,592 m is NTB's figure for the hill; the NAA site lists 1,450 m for the Sarangkot site. Toripani altitude not found.
Number of operating companies varies by source (45-74).
